summary: Verified Railway cron 401 diagnostic fix on POST /api/admin/jobs/run-daily-invoicing against LIVE backend (https://db-bridge-5.preview.emergentagent.com). All 3 primary auth cases + 4 regression cases PASS (7/7). The diagnostic branch in _require_cron_token() correctly detects the raw-secret-as-bearer failure mode and returns a clear message; valid signed JWT is accepted; missing token is rejected with the exact expected detail; and no sibling failure modes were cannibalised (wrong-secret, wrong-audience, wrong-scope, expired-token still return the correct status + detail).

CASE1_raw_secret_as_bearer.actual_detail: Cron token malformed — expected a signed JWT (3 dot-separated segments). Check the cron command mints a JWT rather than posting the secret directly.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal, well-scoped, and correctly placed inside the jwt.PyJWTError branch of _require_cron_token — it only intercepts strings that PyJWT already failed to parse, so it cannot accidentally mask legitimate JWT verification errors.
Diagnostic message is actionable and points to the runbook — good operator ergonomics for Railway logs.

test_daily_invoicing.py mixes auth-only tests with DB-mutating tests behind a single ALLOW_ATTACK_SIM guard. Consider splitting auth tests into their own file (as done in test_cron_auth_only.py) so CI can regress the auth surface without touching Supabase.
seed_data_creation: None — auth-only tests do not mutate the DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The DB-mutating invoice/reminder branch tests in /app/backend/tests/test_daily_invoicing.py were intentionally NOT executed (out of scope per review request). To run them, set ALLOW_ATTACK_SIM=1 and pytest that file. Auth-only regression lives in /app/backend/tests/test_cron_auth_only.py and can be run without any guard.
rca of the issue: Railway cron was configured with `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_JOB_JWT_SECRET` instead of minting a signed HS256 JWT. PyJWT tried to base64-decode the raw urlsafe secret as a JWT header and raised an inscrutable UTF-8 codec error. The fix (daily_invoicing.py:93-107) inspects the credential inside the PyJWTError branch — if it doesn't have exactly 2 dots (i.e. is not a 3-segment JWT), it raises a specific 401 with 'Cron token malformed — expected a signed JWT (3 dot-separated segments)' message. Verified against live backend: raw secret → clear diagnostic 401; valid JWT → 200; no token → 'Cron bearer token required.' 401; all sibling failure modes intact.
